newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firm, CFDs up 5 cts, mogas towed up.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firm, CFDs up 5 cts, mogas towed up.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed on Monday , extending gains made on Friday.
Dealers said demand in Asia for gas oil and a firmer tone on Brent futures again lifted the wider European market.

Brent crude CFDs rose about five cents a barrel for this week's dates after a jump of 13 cts a barrel last Friday. This week was valued at about 43 cents under June compared to talk around 63 cents under a week ago.
The following three weeks were pegged at 39 cents, 37 cents and 34 cents under respectively.

Gasoline swaps rose $1 a tonne, dragged higher by firm Brent futures. A single Rotterdam barge traded at $194 for 1-15 May but no swaps were heard. May was pegged just above $195 with June about $3 lower.

Heavy fuel climbed $1 a tonne to talk around $84 for May barges. June was $1 higher but dealers said the thin physical market had dampened trade. Just two barges had traded at $83.25 and $83.50. Low sulphur was valued around $89 for May but no trade was heard.
Gas oil against Brent held at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums were flat after edging higher late last week. May was bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
